The flush_lock semantics are as intended. lock_shared blocks on creation of the lock file. If creation fails there is an error, not simply a lock to wait on.

text: The flush lock exists *only* to cause a lock file to be left behind in the event of an uncontrolled shutdown. The lock is tested on startup, preventing execution in the case of a preceding uncontrolled shutdown.

elements.text: The original simple startup/shutdown use of the lock is straightforward. However write flushing is essentially transactional commit. In v3 this could be guarded in each data file write independently. However v4 incorporates multi-file transactions, materially complicating write flushing. As you can see the lock attempts are not guarded, so the class is not thread safe across the shared lock file resource. In order to properly support transactional commit the class needs to accept a flush mutex and use it to apply an upgradeable lock around the lock file access. This will allow the flush lock to become an actual guard for transactional commit.

elements.text: The idea is to isolate validation to a pure functional operation over a data set. The presumption is that the data set (chain) is stored and reproduced faithfully (presumed to be consensus behavior). Validation of an object is broken into context free and contextual (requiring population from other objects), with all validation methods on the objects themselves. The validation classes invoke validation and manage the determination of relative strength of a given branch. By objects self-validating against their own metadata, testing full validation becomes straightforward (functional).

Hello there, I'd like to ask for a clarification for a project I'm working on which make use of libbitcoin-system v3.
I need to sign a coinjoin tx, which can spend utxos of types p2pkh, p2sh-p2wpkh, bech32(native-p2wpkh).
As per my understanding, if I don't want to use the SIGHASH_ANYONECANPAY every input has to be signed "togheter with his siblings".
To do this I need to create a input::list and then call tx.set_inputs(that_list) and then sign them one by one using script::create_endorsement. I saw that what create_endorsement do in the generate_signature_hash step is basically creating a copy of the tx stripping away the scriptSig from the others inputs and replacing the scriptSig of the input that has to be signed with the prev_out.scriptPubKey, which is perfectly fine.
Now that I have the endorsement... how can I safely set the "real" input (the one in the tx.inputs_) scriptSig? The transaction header file says that using a reference to the tx.inputs_ is deprecated and unsafe (<https://github.com/libbitcoin/libbitcoin-system/blob/version3/include/bitcoin/bitcoin/chain/transaction.hpp> line 130).
My question is: how can I sign multiple inputs with SIGHASH_ALL (without making use of SIGHASH_ANYONECANPAY) using safe endpoints only? I feel like I'm missing something, but can't guess what.
Sorry for my terrible english and maybe a bit confused explanation.
